subject: Stacked commitments — preemption & handover guidelines for overlapping tranches
messages:
From: Rohit Jain <rohit.jain@auroracloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helix.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Overlap: Aurora enterprise tranche + Helix pilot — urgent guidance needed

Sean —

Quick heads up from our side: two commitments are converging on the same week in late July. Our Enterprise reserved pool (AUR-5921) ramps to full commit on July 22; Helix (pilot, small but latency-sensitive) needs a burst window July 24–28 as part of their go-live. Both were sold as non-preemptible lanes for Aurora, but Helix was sold with a soft-latency SLA that requires colocated GPUs.

We need a clear answer on what will happen if demand spikes: can Helix be bumped to a nearby region? Should we expect preemption? We need a decision to tell procurement and schedule the migration effort. Attaching our estimated CPU/GPU footprint.

—Rohit
AuroraCloud, Sr. Infrastructure PM

Attachments: aurora_capacity_matrix_q2_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 340KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rohit Jain <rohit.jain@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Overlap: Aurora enterprise tranche + Helix pilot — urgent guidance needed

Rohit —

Thanks for the heads up and for the matrix. I’m looping in Ops and our Deals lead to map commitments. Short answer: we can avoid service disruption with a deterministic preemption plan and a scheduled handover window, but I want to propose the explicit steps so everyone has certainty: 

1) Confirm hard reserved GPU pool for AUR-5921 through July 31 (per contract), but allow a measured burst reservation for Helix with limits.
2) If utilization exceeds 92% sustained for >10m on July 24–28, apply prioritized preemption rules: non-critical short-burst jobs -> preempt first.
3) If preemption is insufficient, invoke scheduled handover: shift Helix to us-west-2 replica for 4 hours while Aurora runs at full capacity; Redwood will cover data egress during the window as a one-time operational credit.

Monica/Ben — can you validate that those control levers are deployable in the runtime and whether the telemetry thresholds are safe?

Sean
Principal, Capacity & Sizing
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Overlap: Aurora enterprise tranche + Helix pilot — urgent guidance needed

Folks —

We can implement the 92% sustained threshold and the prioritized preemption class within the runtime. Notes: 
- Preemption policy needs to be pinned to job tags generated at admission (deal_id tags).
- We should pre-warm the us-west-2 fleet for Helix to reduce migration latency; that requires a 48–72 hour warmup if we plan GPU cache priming.
- I recommend a rehearsal run on July 10: spin Helix replica and run a synthetic traffic profile to validate KV cache warmup and latency.

I’ll push a ticket to infra ops and share playbook steps.

Monica
Director, Runtime Ops

> On Jun 15, 2028, at 10:04, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> > Monica/Ben — can you validate that those control levers are deployable in the runtime and whether the telemetry thresholds are safe?

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Overlap: Aurora enterprise tranche + Helix pilot — urgent guidance needed

Agree with the approach. Two practical constraints: 
- Our autoscaler will respect reserved commitments; we need an explicit "burst pool" carve for Helix that is time-bound. I can create that carve and tag it to deal Helix-PILOT-001.
- If we do the one-time egress credit, ops still needs a signed approval from Sales (finance sign-off as well). Who will own customer communication?

Karthik — can you estimate the additional GPU-hours for the warmup window? I want to include it in the carve request.

Ben
Sr. Sales Engineer

> On Jun 15, 2028, at 11:22, Monica Patel wrote:
> > I recommend a rehearsal run on July 10...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Overlap: Aurora enterprise tranche + Helix pilot — urgent guidance needed

Ben — estimate below for warmup and burst carve (ballpark):
- Warmup footprint (us-west-2 pre-warm, 48h): 8 A100x80 GPU-hours * 48 = 384 GPU-hours (cache priming + model sharding ops).
- Burst window (4h full pilot peak): 24 GPUs * 4h = 96 GPU-hours.
- Safety margin + buffer jobs: +20% => ~580 GPU-hours total.

If Redwood covers the warmup and egress credit as a customer experience concession, I can size the carve accordingly. Otherwise, Aurora or Helix cover the warmup line-item.

Karthik
Solutions Architect

From: Rohit Jain <rohit.jain@auroracloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Overlap: Aurora enterprise tranche + Helix pilot — urgent guidance needed

Sean / team —

Thanks for the quick triage. Aurora is willing to accept the scheduled handover to us-west-2 for the four-hour window, provided the handover is executed with clear runbook steps and that Redwood certifies no long-tail performance regression after the migration. We also need the rehearsal run as Monica suggested (July 10 works).

We will not sign up for additional line items for warmup — we'd prefer Redwood to absorb the warmup and egress credit. If finance needs an approval note for the concession, loop in your sales ops and finance.

Rohit

> On Jun 15, 2028, at 14:05, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> > If Redwood covers the warmup and egress credit as a customer experience concession...

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rohit Jain <rohit.jain@auroracloud.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Overlap: Aurora enterprise tranche + Helix pilot — urgent guidance needed

Team / Rohit —

Decision summary and next steps: 
1) Redwood will absorb the warmup GPU-hours (estimate 384 GPU-hours) and the one-time egress credit for the 4-hour handover window as a customer experience concession tied to AUR-5921. This will be logged as a non-recurring operational credit.
2) We will implement the 92% sustained telemetry threshold and prioritized preemption class; Monica will own runtime controls/tickets.
3) Ben will scope and create a time-bound burst carve (Helix-PILOT-001) and send the approval note to Sales Ops & Finance for the one-off charge paperwork (even though Redwood will absorb cost, we need a paper trail).
4) Monica/Ops will run the rehearsal on July 10 at 09:00 PT. Monica — please post the runbook link and validation checklist to the shared Drive.

Rohit — thanks for flexibility. We’ll send a short runbook and the post-rehearsal report so Aurora can sign off on production readiness.

Sean
Principal, Capacity & Sizing
Redwood Inference

Attachments: preemption_policy_v1.pdf (policy excerpt, 12 pages)
